title: bl_procs.running never signals a pid on Windows, so no caller can end a process by probing it
goal: bl_procs.running returns None on Windows (os.name nt) without calling os.kill, the one place every caller's liveness probe goes through, instead of each call site carrying its own os.name guard
notes: SP-razcgjsb retrospective 2026-10-20: the review's S1 BG-r3mpv76o: ST-wubbd6ws added a live-workers test in mon_sessions.session_rows without the os.name guard its two sibling branches in the same function had, so the sessions panel would os.kill(pid, 0) a worker on Windows, which ends it. ST-yozfikuv's gate recorded 'null on Windows' but nothing enforced it at the one helper all callers use. What let it through: the guard lived at each call site; no check planted os.name nt for the new branch.
